quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without stopping suddenly. Sudden stops can cause drivers behind you to hit your vehicle.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should only reduce your speed to 35 mph if the weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign where you see it.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could make it unsafe to drive. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
Fix the problem when you have money to do so.
Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that could affect safe driving must be fixed right away. Fix it before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: If you hit a parked car, what should you do?

options.text: Wait at the scene until the owner comes back.
Try to find the owner, or leave a note with your name, phone number, and the time and date of the accident.
Leave your name and address at the local courthouse.
Call a tow truck to remove the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to find the owner, or leave a note with your name, phone number, and the time and date of the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, you must try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a visible note with your contact information and the date and time of the accident.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body process in one hour?

options.text: Half a drink.
One drink.
Two drinks.
Three drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: Your body needs about one hour to process one alcoholic drink.

questions.question: How can you stay awake on long driving trips?

options.text: Turn on the car radio.
Drive slower.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: They can be safely held by an adult.
They can stand on the floor in the back seat.
They will be safe in an accident because they are small.
They must always be properly secured in a child seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must always be properly secured in a child seat.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are needed for small children. No adult can hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Children must always be properly restrained in a seat.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If your vehicle is completely off the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They make no errors.
They have trouble driving slowly.
They become better drivers.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their cars.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the way is clear.
Stop completely before going forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are going the wrong way on a one-way street. You risk a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Has a triangle shape.
Is blue with black letters.
Shows the recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows the recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn warning signs often show a recommended speed for drivers on those curves and turns. Even if you feel safe going faster in good weather, you should never do so in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the main road. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: This sign prevents:

options.text: Entering full parking lots.
Entering road construction areas.
Entering dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic moves one way only. You must not enter from your current direction.

questions.question: When there are no signs or lane markings for turning, you should:

options.text: Stop before turning.
Turn from the lane closest to your desired direction.
Turn from the center lane.
Turn from any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn from the lane closest to your desired direction.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to where you want to go, and turn into the lane closest to your starting lane.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal has the same rules as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all traffic that does not have to stop go first.

questions.question: If your brakes fail, you should first:

options.text: Shift the transmission into neutral.
Pump the brake pedal several times to build up brake pressure.
Flash your lights at other drivers.
Jump out of the vehicle right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal several times to build up brake pressure.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail, pump the pedal several times. This often builds up enough pressure to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move the injured person unless you must. Moving them wrong can make minor injuries serious. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders when the opposite lane is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car in front. Your vehicle will take longer to stop than it does on dry roads.

questions.question: You must drive carefully near a pedestrian using a white cane because:

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, let them cross safely, and be ready to stop. Be very careful not to hit them.

questions.question: A green arrow and a red light mean:

options.text: You can only drive straight.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only go the way the arrow points. Make sure the intersection is clear before you drive.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol hurts your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Even a little alcohol makes you a worse driver. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: Left arm extended upward means the driver is turning right. If you are following this driver, watch for the turn and adjust your driving.

questions.question: This sign means you should:

options.text: Follow the detour to the right.
Get ready to enter a one-way street.
Stay on the main highway if you can.
Follow the detour to the right only if it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the detour to the right.
questions.explanation: Detour signs are orange with black letters or symbols. They show you an alternate route because the main road is blocked by construction. You must follow the detour.
